clue.text: Break for the star to get made up

indicators.note: made up as in composed afresh, so the letters of the two words are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a holiday and visits the make-up artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get made up' reshuffles the letters of THE STAR. 'Break' looks like a holiday noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something is to smash or break it into pieces.

clue.text: Extensive period of incarceration

explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of land is an extensive expanse, and a stretch is also slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Damned dogs indeed!

parts.note: a word for cursed that literally carries a word for mongrels inside it, so the dogs are damned in deed

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at some wretched hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for damned has CURS, dogs, sitting within it, hence the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurst is an archaic spelling meaning doomed or under a curse.

clue.text: Stumble bearing rubbish

parts.note: to trip is to stumble
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Tripping while carrying a load of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal, used informally to mean nonsense or worthless stuff.

clue.text: This rogue might be made trustworthy

indicators.note: might be made into something else, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Reforming a scoundrel into an honest citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright, hence honest and reliable.

clue.text: Struggled to go without rest when called on

indicators.note: to go outside, so the word for struggled is placed around the word for rest

parts.note: struggled or competed means vied
to rest is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone who fought on without a break when visitors called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go without' reads as doing without, but 'without' here means outside: VIED wraps around SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Called on is an idiom for paying a visit to someone.

clue.text: The Minister of Transport behind certain figures

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the vehicle follows the figures

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A government transport chief lagging behind the statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Minister of Transport' reads as a government post, but 'Minister' is the clergyman and CAR is the transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Greatly shocked, gets grade reassessed

indicators.note: a grade that is reassessed is changed, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A student is stunned when the mark is reviewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered means astonished, as though knocked off balance.

clue.text: Picture expert accommodated by a Greek character

indicators.note: accommodated by means housed within, so the word for expert goes inside the letter

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: An art specialist staying with a Greek host.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or picturesque group, like a painting.

clue.text: Some unseated rider, angered and upset

indicators.note: some of these words means only part of them supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A rider thrown from the saddle is angry and distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder, to unsettle or disturb.

clue.text: Unstable but fabulous old bird, the top man!

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian fable
a king is the man at the top of a realm

explanation.surface: A wobbly but legendary old character who is still the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocking is swaying back and forth, so not steady.

clue.text: Small child given caution makes room

parts.note: CH is a short form of child
the amber traffic light is the caution signal before red

explanation.surface: A youngster told to be careful creates space.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBER is the British traffic light between green and red, signalling caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a synonym for a room, especially a formal or private one.

clue.text: A fellow plaguing people in high places

indicators.note: the word for people sits inside the pair of words for high places

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, so two of them give TOR and TOR
men is a plain word for people

explanation.surface: A man pestering the powerful and well-placed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high places' is plural, giving two TORs, with MEN placed between them. TORS are rocky hilltops on English moors such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps plaguing others is a persecutor who inflicts torment.

clue.text: Concerned about the environment, but easily fooled

explanation.surface: An eco-warrior who is also rather gullible.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means ecologically minded in politics, and also naive or inexperienced, as a green recruit is gullible.

clue.text: Overwrought guy put out

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man or guy

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered, so the letters of the little word put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stressed man who has been inconvenienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal idiom for agitated and anxious.

clue.text: Sort of pay muddle-create new structure

parts.note: pie is printer's jargon for a muddle of type

indicators.note: giving a word a new structure rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Confused plans to restructure the wage system.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE (also spelt pi) is jumbled printing type; 'new structure' rearranges CREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece rate is a wage system paying a fixed sum per item produced.

clue.text: Suitable work left with a French female

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
port is the left side of a ship
une is the French feminine form of 'a'

explanation.surface: A job that would suit someone left alone with a French woman.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the sailor's word for left; UNE is French for 'a' before a feminine noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed and so appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Take steps to get it working

definitions.text: Take steps to get it working

parts.words: Take steps to get it working
parts.note: read literally, the device only functions when its wearer walks, counting every pace

explanation.surface: Advice to act so as to make something function.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a gadget that counts the walker's paces.

clue.text: The crowd sitting in the tall grass kept under control

indicators.note: one word sits within another, here the crowd inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
a press is a dense crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Spectators hiding in long grass are kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress feelings or people is to hold them down or restrain them.

clue.text: One enters to honour 19

indicators.note: the letter for one goes into the word for honour

parts.note: to revere is to honour or venerate
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone walks in to pay respect to a vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of absorbed musing.

clue.text: Useful information for a director?

explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a helpful tip, and literally something that points the way, like a signpost.

clue.text: Armed revolutionary's vision

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning over, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gun-toting rebel's view of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision is something seen in the mind, like a fantasy during sleep.

clue.text: Accord the right style

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give someone a right to something, and also to give a name or title.

clue.text: What the pitman got with a pound

definitions.text: What the pitman got with a pound

parts.note: a pitman works down a pit, a coal miner
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A coal worker's earnings came with a pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: what a miner extracts is ore or coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner digs ore and coal, natural inorganic substances from the earth.

clue.text: Speak evil about none

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for evil goes round the letter for none

parts.note: vice is wickedness or evil
O is zero, nothing or none

explanation.surface: A call to speak out against wickedness, and no one does.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it or say it out loud.

clue.text: Not involved not turning over dope

parts.note: simple means uncomplicated, not involved

indicators.note: turning over signals the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Someone detached and unchanging, perhaps a sluggish fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses NOT to TON. 'dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a stupid person or fool.

clue.text: The fish was off

explanation.definitionFit: The smelt is a small silvery sea fish, and smelt is a past form of smell, as food that has gone bad.

clue.text: Skinny skinhead heels

parts.note: lean means thin or skinny

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word it is attached to

explanation.surface: A thin shaven-headed youth in heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a youth but splits as head of skin. 'heels' is the verb, as a ship heels over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels tilts to one side, as something that tilts or slopes over.

clue.text: Desert tribe's competitive activity

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
a race is a people or tribe

explanation.surface: A nomadic people of the desert compete with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy noun but is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the relentless competitive struggle of working life.

clue.text: Made to flower using heating equipment

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Encouraging a plant to bloom with a heater.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is a kitchen appliance that browns bread by heating it.

clue.text: Purposeful letters are sent all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Determined correspondence has gone out everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges ARE and SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and determined in intent.

clue.text: Famous philosopher almost certain to back deal

indicators.note: to back means to go backwards, so the shortened word is reversed
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
to sell is to deal in goods

explanation.surface: A great thinker is fairly sure he will support the agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims SURE to SUR, which 'to back' reverses to RUS. Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher and logician.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell was a celebrated twentieth-century British philosopher and logician.
